title: Progressive failover decision lane — customer brief (draft)
summary: Working draft for a short statuspage update + customer-facing post-incident brief that presents the progressive failover choices we made during the 2026-12-07 inference disruption and clearly lists customer options (safe-mode, replay, or accept fallthrough). This doc is intended to be the canonical customer communication used by CS and account teams for tenants that requested more detail.
intended_audience: Primary: customers impacted by model fallthroughs and degraded streaming. Secondary: account teams, SRE, product ops for alignment before publish.
statuspage_update_draft: Incident: Progressive failover engaged in EU region — partial degradation affecting streaming responses. Start: 2026-12-07 08:41 UTC. Impact: Some requests routed to fallback model variants with longer latency and occasionally truncated structured outputs for up to 40% of requests in a subset of tenants. What we did: We activated a progressive failover lane to maintain availability while we investigated root cause; automatically routed traffic to smaller-capacity compatible variants and applied a temporary throttling policy to reduce KV cache pressure. Customer impact: possible slower responses and occasional truncated JSON outputs. Next steps: we will roll back to primary model variants after cache stabilization and full verification (ETA 2–6 hours). If you prefer a safe-mode (no fallthrough), reply to this message and we will pin your tenant to primary-only routing while we complete stabilization. Contact: support@redwood.com or your TAM. Apology: We know this affected production experiences for some teams — we’re prioritizing verification and preserving output integrity.
short-email-update:
Subject: Brief update — regional progressive failover in EU (Dec 7)

Hi — quick update for teams using Redwood in EU regions. At 08:41 UTC we observed a KV cache pressure event that caused a subset of inference requests to be routed to fallback model variants. We enabled a progressive failover lane to keep requests returning responses while we stabilize. Expected effect: higher latency and occasional truncated structured outputs for some calls. We expect to revert the lane after verification (ETA 2–6 hours). If you want us to opt your tenant into safe-mode (no fallback), reply and we’ll act. Full customer brief and verification steps will follow. — Aisha (CS)
postmortem_customer_summary: Root cause (summary): A sustained KV cache eviction storm on the serving runtime in EU-west triggered routing heuristics that preferentially shifted traffic to smaller, quantized model variants. This was compounded by an autoscaling weight bug that slowed cache refill. Result: progressive failover engaged and some streaming sessions experienced truncation or increased latency. What we changed immediately: 1) Disabled automatic autoscale adjustment that was mismatching cache warmup profiles. 2) Increased ephemeral KV cache capacity on hot nodes and applied targeted cache warming for high-QPS tenants. 3) Rebalanced routing weight to prefer primary variants as cache warmed. Why we made the choices: keeping live responses (even at lower quality) with clear customer opt-outs reduced total request failures and allowed some customers to continue serving traffic. Verification: we validated token-level parity sampling on a subset of requests and observed restored sequence completion rates to baseline after 105 minutes. Corrective actions (near-term): rolling patch to fix autoscale-weighting bug (deploy v1.0.3), introduce a cache-warmup gating check before allowing automatic scale-down, and add a tenant-visible flag with self-serve safe-mode. Long-term: algorithmic improvements to routing policy, improved canary coverage for cache pressure scenarios, and expanded observability for early detection of KV eviction storms.
recommended_customer_actions:
- If you rely on strict structured outputs (JSON schemas), opt into safe-mode: no fallthrough to smaller models. This prevents truncation but may increase latency or errors until we fully stabilize. To opt in: reply to this email or open a support ticket with 'SAFE-MODE REQUEST'.
- If you experienced missing or truncated outputs and want a replay of affected calls: provide a date/time range and sample request ids (we will prioritize enterprise replay queue). Replays are optional — we can also offer a targeted reconciliation report.
- Rate-limiting/backoff: consider brief client-side exponential backoff (250ms -> cap 2s) for streaming clients during our stabilization window.
- Contact: support@redwood.com or your TAM for tenant-specific fixes and credit discussions.
operator_playbook_snippet:
Ops quick checklist (for SRE/Oncall):
1) Identify hot nodes: query kv_eviction_rate > threshold across EU clusters.
2) Temporarily apply targeted cache increase: set cache_capacity_multiplier=1.5 for nodes with eviction spikes.
3) Disable autoscale-weighting patch via feature flag: routing.autoscale_adjust=false.
4) Validate: sample 100 calls across impacted tenants and confirm sequence completion rate >= 95% before gradual rollback.
5) Notify CS channel and update status page with rollback ETA.
Notes: The safe-mode pin should be applied per-tenant in routing config and excluded from autoscale adjustments.

open_questions_and_risks:
- Need to confirm whether a specific tenant traffic pattern (bursting small-context chat) materially accelerated local KV churn; CS to collect tenant patterns.
- Risk: If autoscale-weighting regression is not fully covered in canaries, similar events could recur; patch requires expanded canary gating.
- Replay volume: estimate queued replay GB and potential cost/throughput to deliver replays within SLA. Product ops to scope.
- Customer opt-in rate for safe-mode could increase latency load on primary nodes; capacity planning needed.

sample_customer_qna:
Q: Will my data be replayed automatically?
A: No — we will not replay tenant traffic without explicit consent. If you request replay, we will coordinate time and scope.
Q: Is model quality permanently affected?
A: No — fallthrough used smaller variants temporarily. After rollback to primary variants and verification, quality metrics returned to baseline.
Q: Will this count as an SLA incident?
A: We're evaluating impact windows on a per-account basis; customers with meaningful degradation may be eligible for credit per contract terms. Please open a ticket if you believe your SLA was breached.
